close_when: Discarded and retained first-input behavior can be separated.
Quartiles and retained counts can be recomputed from raw rows.
Raw retained rows exist in the topology where the decision will be made.
Run order, branch order, and warmup phase are recorded.
Failures, retries, skipped rows, and actionability waits are joined to metric rows.
Resource groups and source-specific readiness are joined to metric rows.
Runner, browser, wp-env, CPU/container, and git/WP identifiers are attached.
The targeted source owner collapses before aggregate timing is cited.
Behavior fixtures pass before timing is interpreted.
Public API, plugin, dynamic dependency, and cross-store cases pass.
Stable key-window IDs and clock sync join sidecars to retained samples.
Observer-on/off rows preserve class ordering and retained counts.
Frequency, residency, QoS, power, runnable latency, or cache counters are joined.
Replay strata or calibrated visual/display endpoints are joined to retained keys.
